correctness.rationale: Tilting the killed symmetric kernel of rate d/2 in each direction gives the factor exp(-lambda t)rho^(j-i); reflection subtracts the kernel from the reflected start. The initial rho^i cancels exactly. In the sine integral, v=u/sqrt(t) and j<=L log(t) permit replacement of sin(jv)/(jv) by one uniformly on bounded u, with Gaussian domination. For diffusive i, evaluation of the remaining Gaussian sine integral gives A_d y exp(-y^2/(2d)), y=i/sqrt(t), in tB_t/j; for i<=t^(1/2-delta), replacing the other sine ratio yields A_d in t^(3/2)B_t/(ij). Bounding both sines linearly also gives the global ij t^(-3/2) bound. Telescoping the Bessel difference for i>=2j uses j indices comparable to i, and shifting the unrestricted Fourier integral by an imaginary h=min(k/(2dt),1) gives the stated t^(-1/2) times exp[-c min(k^2/t,k)] bound. These estimates control the large-i tail; the global bound makes the small-diffusive-i remainder O(epsilon^(2-beta)) below beta=2. The weighted diffusive Riemann sum then gives the normalized gamma transformation in the finding. At beta=2 the harmonic sum up to t^u contributes u log(t) for 0<u<1/2, the total contributes (1/2)log(t), and the mass above sqrt(t) is lower order. At beta>2 the global bound is summable against i^(-beta)rho^j; counting-measure dominated convergence gives total variation after normalization. The terminal tail j>L log(t) is negligible by the geometric majorant, and in each regime the joint restricted weights factor with j rho^j. The terminal normalization is rho/(1-rho)^2. In the QSD recurrence a pi_(j+1)+b pi_(j-1)=(a+b-theta)pi_j with pi_0=0, theta=lambda gives the positive double-root solution j rho^j; larger theta cannot give positive weights, and smaller theta gives a larger law by an increasing likelihood ratio relative to j rho^j. Thus the identification as the minimal QSD is correct. The two frozen scripts and recorded results were inspected, not executed; no finite probe substitutes for the uniform limits.

value.rationale: The result identifies which starting states account for survival even when the terminal law is unchanged. It distinguishes diffusive, logarithmically spread and lattice-localized entrances with exact limits and shows they decouple from the terminal site. In particular the log-uniform threshold law contains information absent from the logarithmic survival prefactor alone.
